edges.description: Inhaled radon progeny irradiate bronchial epithelium with alpha particles, but the cited evidence is deliberately hedged and is qualified to current smokers at high residential concentrations, with the risk in never-smokers left unresolved. Recorded as a susceptibility contribution rather than an established mutational route.

Coal-smoke polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons — principally benzo[a]pyrene and methylated PAHs such as 5-methylchrysene — are the exposures that best explain risk in this population, and the resulting tumours carry a correspondingly distinct mutational spectrum: excess C:G to A:T transversions, a markedly higher mutated-gene count than tumours from control regions, and a BaP-attributed EGFR-G719X hotspot. The edge is typed INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES rather than DIRECT because the intervening steps (PAH metabolic activation, bulky DNA adduct formation, error-prone bypass) are established chemistry that this entry does not model as its own nodes; the Xuanwei-specific attribution itself rests on mutational-signature inference, not on experimental demonstration in these patients.

The chip reads out driver-kinase-dependent therapeutic response, reproducing the tyrosine kinase inhibitor sensitivity seen in patients and resolving EGFR- and MET-mediated modulation of that response by the mechanical microenvironment.
edges.limitations: Only EGFR and MET signalling were implicated; the ALK and ROS1 rearrangement arms of this node were not modelled. The published abstract reports lung cancer cell lines in a reconstituted microenvironment rather than patient-derived tumour carrying its native driver spectrum, so allele-level genotype-response relationships are not established by this system.
edges.source: Human orthotopic NSCLC lung organ-on-chip (Wyss Institute)

edges.description: The chip reconstitutes an orthotopic lung microenvironment in which tumour growth and dormancy are microenvironment-specific, and adds the mechanical dimension of breathing motion that static culture cannot supply.
edges.limitations: The microenvironment modelled is epithelial and mechanical. The abstract reports no immune, myeloid or fibroblast compartment, so the immune-remodelling and desmoplastic facets of this node are outside what the system captures.
edges.source: Human orthotopic NSCLC lung organ-on-chip (Wyss Institute)

edges.description: Local invasion of lung cancer cells is measurable in the chip and is sensitive to breathing-associated mechanical cues.
edges.limitations: Only the local invasive step is represented. The system has no circulation, distant organ site, or colonisation compartment, so intravasation, survival in transit and metastatic outgrowth - the steps that make this node clinically decisive - are not modelled.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of lung cancer associated with domestic use of coal in Xuanwei, China: retrospective cohort study.
evidence.snippet: In Xuanwei, the domestic use of smoky coal is associated with a substantial increase in the absolute lifetime risk of developing lung cancer and is likely to represent one of the strongest effects of environmental pollution reported for cancer risk.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of lung cancer associated with domestic use of coal in Xuanwei, China: retrospective cohort study.
evidence.snippet: The absolute risks of lung cancer death before 70 years of age for men and women using smoky coal were 18% and 20%, respectively, compared with less than 0.5% among smokeless coal users of both sexes.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of Somatic Mutations in Air Pollution-Related Lung Cancer.
evidence.snippet: In Xuanwei City of Yunnan Province, the lung cancer incidence is among the highest in China attributed to severe air pollution generated by combustion of smoky coal

nodes.description: Microfluidic human lung organ chip in which non-small-cell lung cancer cells are grown within a reconstituted human lung microenvironment under cyclic mechanical actuation that mimics breathing motions. A non-animal New Approach Methodology that reproduces organ-microenvironment-specific tumour growth, tumour dormancy and tyrosine kinase inhibitor responses in vitro, and that resolves the influence of physical breathing cues on EGFR and MET signalling.

nodes.description: Cancer cells spread from the primary tumor site to distant organs, commonly to the brain, bones, liver, and adrenal glands.

evidence.reference_title: The landscape of small cell lung cancer metastases: Organ specificity and timing.
evidence.snippet: Our results are suggestive for particular site- and sequence-specific metastasis patterns in human SCLC. SCLC bone metastases tend to appear together with liver metastases, while brain metastases occur together with adrenal gland metastases.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical approach of non-small cell lung cancer with extrapulmonary metastasis.
evidence.snippet: Nearly 75% of patients have a disseminated carcinoma at diagnosis. Up to 50% of patients with a localized disease will develop metastasis. Nevertheless, the current scientific evidence has demonstrated that when the metastatic disease is limited, particularly in specific locations such as the brain and the adrenal glands, a multidisciplinary approach with radical intent could achieve a longer survival.

evidence.reference_title: CXCR4/CXCL12 in non-small-cell lung cancer metastasis to the brain.
evidence.snippet: At least one third of the people with lung cancer develop brain metastases at some point during their disease, even often before the diagnosis of lung cancer is made. The high rate of brain metastasis makes lung cancer the most common type of tumor to spread to the brain.

evidence.reference_title: Management and Treatment of Non-small Cell Lung Cancer with MET Alteration and Mechanisms of Resistance.
evidence.snippet: Pathologic activation of MET can be achieved with increased number of gene copies overexpression, or decreased protein degradation through several mechanisms, including mutations, amplifications, or fusions. Besides its role as primary driver, MET activation might also mediate resistance to kinase inhibitors in NSCLC with various other actionable alterations.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in EGFR best illustrate the therapeutic relevance of molecular classification. This article reviews the scope of presently known driving molecular alterations, including ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, HER2 and PIK3CA, with a special emphasis on aLK rearrangements, and outlines their potential therapeutic applications.

evidence.reference_title: Oncogene addicted non-small-cell lung cancer: current standard and hot topics.
evidence.snippet: Activating mutations in the EGFR and rearrangements in the anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) or ROS proto-oncogene 1 receptor tyrosine kinase (ROS1) genes have been identified as oncogenic drivers in non-small-cell lung cancer.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic determinants of lung cancer: Understanding the oncogenic potential of somatic missense mutations.
evidence.snippet: The aim of the current study is to extract meaningful information from the online somatic mutation data (retrieved from cBioPortal) of 16 most significantly mutated oncogenes in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), namely EGFR, NRAS, KRAS, HER2 (ERBB2), RET, MET, ROS1, FGFR1, BRAF ... for improving our understanding of the pathobiology of the lung cancer.

evidence.reference_title: Uncommon EGFR Mutations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Their Impact on the Treatment.
evidence.snippet: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations play an important role in the pathogenesis of non-small cell lung cancer. ... In patients with EGFR mutations, a significant improvement in therapeutic outcomes was achieved with the administration of targeted therapy using tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Epidemiology of the Main Druggable Genetic Alterations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Testing the presence of driver mutations in specific genes in lung tumors has thus radically changed the clinical management and outcomes of the disease. ... namely EGFR, KRAS, BRAF, MET, and HER2 mutations or amplification, as well as ALK and ROS1 fusions.

evidence.snippet: Based on the most recent findings, there is some evidence that radon may contribute to lung cancer risk in current smokers in high residential radon environments... The situation regarding the risk of lung cancer from radon in non-smokers (ex and never) is unclear.

evidence.snippet: Miners increased risk of contracting lung cancer is included. It is concluded that the mine ventilation system satisfies the conditions required by the current radiological protection of the miners.

evidence.snippet: Human lung cancers are phenotypically more diverse and broadly constitute 2 types... small cell lung cancers and nonsmall cell lung cancers (NSCLCs). ... especially in lung cancers resulting from exposure to environmental carcinogens.
